description: Async Python client for blockchain explorer APIs (Etherscan, BlockScout, NodeReal) with one interface, guaranteed-complete pagination and exact Wei math.
rules: The public API is ChainscanClient only. Construct it with ChainscanClient.from_config(scanner, network) inside an 'async with' block. There is no legacy Client class, facade, or URL builder.
get_* methods return ONE page. For complete data call get_all_* (materialized) or iter_*_streaming (constant memory). A transactions page holds ~50-100 items; a logs page is capped at ~1000.
Balances, values and supplies are Wei strings. Convert with wei_to_ether() or to_decimal_amount() for exact Decimal math. Never write int(wei) / 10**18 - float division loses precision.

get_all_* and iter_*_streaming default to guarantee_complete=True: they return every matching record or raise (PaginationDataLossError, CompletenessUnavailableError). Do not implement manual page/offset loops to work around provider caps.

Scanner coverage differs: etherscan v2 declares all 33 methods (needs ETHERSCAN_KEY), blockscout v1 declares 31 keyless, blockscout_v2 declares 11 keyless with cursor pagination, nodereal declares 25 on BSC only. An undeclared method raises MethodNotDeclaredError.
API keys are resolved from the environment or .env by ConfigurationManager. Do not hardcode keys or pass them as literals in example code.

Raw responses are provider-native. Code that must run against several providers should use the *_normalized variants (get_all_transactions_normalized, iter_logs_normalized, ...), which return typed frozen dataclasses from aiochainscan.domain.normalized.
For provider failover use ChainscanPool.from_config([(scanner, network), ...]) - it exposes the full ChainscanClient surface and switches providers only on fallback-eligible failures.
Use Utf8 (string) columns for Wei in DataFrames. Int64 overflows above ~9.2 ETH.
